answer.effective_date: March 7, 2026 (published 11/21/2025); this is the version in force as of the 2026-08-21 denial date. (Prior version, V1.0.2025, was effective July 1, 2025; a July 2026 update round did not list CMM-315 as changed, so V2.0.2025 remains current.)
criteria_quotes: "These guidelines apply to services or supplies managed by EviCore for Cigna as outlined by the Cigna CPT list." (confirms CMM-315 is the delegated medical-necessity document Cigna uses for CPT 29827)
Table of contents confirms the relevant sections: 'Rotator Cuff Repair — Indications' (p. 26) and 'Rotator Cuff Repair — Non-Indications' (p. 28) of CMM-315 V2.0.2025.

From the policy's General Guidelines section (verified verbatim): 'The determination of medical necessity for the performance of shoulder surgery is always made on a case-by-case basis.' and 'Manipulation of a shoulder joint under general anesthesia is included in all arthroscopic shoulder procedures and is therefore considered incidental to the base procedure requiring medical necessity review.'

From the Rotator Cuff Tear definitions (verified verbatim), which the reviewer applies when reading imaging: 'Evaluation of rotator cuff muscle quality with CT or MRI is an important consideration. Chronic and larger tears are associated with muscle atrophy and fatty replacement, both of which correlate with inferior functional outcome after rotator cuff repair,' and the tear-size classification scheme (Ellman partial-thickness grades 1-3; Cofield full-thickness small/medium/large/massive) that the imaging report is measured against.

By analogy to the adjacent, fully-verified 'Diagnostic Arthroscopy Indications' section of the same document (same ALL/ANY format used throughout CMM-315), medical necessity determinations in this policy generally require: imaging findings correlated with exam findings, function-limiting symptoms of a specified minimum duration, and documented failure of a minimum duration of provider-directed non-surgical management, with other diagnoses excluded — but I could NOT retrieve the literal bullet list for the Rotator Cuff Repair Indications section itself (pages 26-28) despite multiple attempts.
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 days from the date of the notice (2026-08-21), i.e., by 2027-02-17, as stated in the denial letter. This matches Cigna's standard published appeal window ('within 180 calendar days of the date of the initial payment or denial notice').
answer.submission_route: 1) Call the Customer Service number on the back of Skyler's Cigna ID card first — the representative can log the appeal and advise if it can be resolved without a formal written appeal. 2) If not resolved, submit a written appeal (Cigna's 'Customer Appeal Request' form or an appeal letter referencing 'Customer Appeal,' plus supporting medical records/imaging and a letter from the surgeon) to the mailing address printed on the ID card/denial notice. Cigna's standard national appeal mailing addresses are: Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8011 (for 'Cigna Network' ID cards) or Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. If the internal appeal is denied, Skyler (on a fully-insured ACA plan) has the right to an independent External Review, which Cigna must describe in the final internal appeal denial letter.
